solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Stretch of land that’s been cleared shows error (8)

annotation.definition: Stretch of land that’s been cleared

blocks.note: to air something is to show it, as a programme is aired
a trip is a slip or mistake

annotation.surface: A land survey spotting a mistake on a newly cleared plot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shows' reads as a verb with 'land' as its subject, but it is the wordplay's first piece. The long definition is fair: planes need exactly such a cleared strip.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a runway in the bush is literally a strip of ground cleared of trees and scrub.

entries.clue: Fire on combustion ultimately out of control? (7)

annotation.definition: Fire on combustion ultimately out of control?

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of 'combustion'
indicatorNotes.out of control: letters that are out of control run wild and lose their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken literally
last letter of combustion
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A blaze that has taken hold and is now raging unchecked.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: as wordplay it jumbles FIRE ON with the N, and read straight it describes a blaze gone wild.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the whole clue, read plainly, describes a fire raging beyond control, which is what the word for a blazing hell means.

entries.clue: Gas around warmer white liquid (6,5)

indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so SCREAM goes around the warmer

blocks.note: a gas or a scream is something hilarious: 'the party was a gas'
an ingle is a fireplace, as in inglenook

annotation.surface: Some gas heater with a pale fluid flowing round it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like fuel for the warmer, but it is slang for a great laugh, a scream. This is the thin pouring cream sold in British shops, as opposed to thick double cream.
annotation.definitionFit: A deliberately vague description: the thinnest British pouring cream is simply a white liquid.

entries.clue: Frost recited — his composition? (5)

indicatorNotes.recited: something recited is spoken, so we hear the word rather than see it

blocks.note: rime is hoar frost

annotation.surface: Robert Frost reading aloud one of his own poems.
annotation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the poet Robert Frost, and 'his composition' plays along, but the wordplay wants frost the weather: rime.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a poet like Frost composes verse, and the question mark flags that a poem is only one kind of composition.

entries.clue: Old kingdom with power over large country (7)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, 'over' puts P above what follows

blocks.note: P = power, as in physics
the largest country in the world

annotation.surface: An ancient realm dominating a vast neighbour.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is historically plausible, since the old German realm was a power in eastern Europe; the letters simply stack P above the big neighbour.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical fact: the Hohenzollern realm centred on Berlin was a kingdom from 1701 until 1918, so it is an old one.

entries.clue: Fogeyish / figure (6)

blocks.note: like an old fogey: stuffy, old-fashioned, uncool
a shape from geometry, here one with four equal sides

annotation.walkthrough: Two unrelated meanings side by side: an adjective for someone stuffy and a noun from geometry.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for conventional and dull, and the four-sided shape.

entries.clue: Captive in luminary, Aristotle, say? (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the captive sits in, inside, the luminary

blocks.note: a shiner is something that shines, a luminary
POW = prisoner of war

annotation.surface: The philosopher Aristotle as a prisoner inside a brilliant mind.
annotation.walkthrough: Aristotle suggests the Greek philosopher, but here it is Aristotle Onassis, the Greek shipping tycoon; the question mark marks him as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Aristotle Onassis made his fortune owning tankers and cargo vessels.

entries.clue: Victoria’s vehicle adorable with roof off (3)

indicatorNotes.with roof off: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: cute = adorable
CUTE loses its first letter, C

annotation.surface: Queen Victoria's sweet little carriage, with its top down.
annotation.walkthrough: Victoria is not the queen but the Australian state, and the vehicle is the Australian pickup truck.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Australia, including the state of Victoria, a utility vehicle or pickup truck goes by this short name.

entries.clue: Reinstate aggregate beneath base (7)

indicatorNotes.beneath: beneath means below, and in a down clue ORE sits below REST

blocks.note: a rest is a support or base, as a snooker cue rest
ore is an aggregate of minerals

annotation.surface: Putting gravel back under a foundation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aggregate' sounds like building gravel beneath a foundation, but it is a mass of minerals dug from the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to put someone or something back in its former place.

entries.clue: Subterfuge / the concern of wags? (5,8)

blocks.note: trickery, underhand goings-on
wags are jokers, and their trade is being amusing

annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: taken literally, the line of work of wits and jokers is comedy.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the idiom for deceptive dealings, and a literal reading as the trade of humour.

entries.clue: Grating, cook last of cheese (6)

indicatorNotes.last of: the last of a word is its final letter, here from cheese

blocks.note: to grill is to cook under direct heat
last letter of cheese

annotation.surface: Grilling the end of a hunk of cheese, perhaps on toast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grating' looks like cheese being grated, which suits the kitchen surface, but it is the noun: a framework of metal bars.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a lattice of bars across an opening.

entries.clue: No words after failing first of papers, a bloomer (8)

indicatorNotes.failing: words that are failing are falling apart, so their letters rearrange
indicatorNotes.first of: the first of a word is its opening letter, here from papers
indicatorNotes.after: after places P behind the jumbled words

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator
first letter of papers

annotation.surface: An exam candidate who failed the first paper, and so a blunderer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A bloomer' reads as a howler after a failed paper, but it means a plant that blooms.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-style definition: an early white spring flower blooms, so it is a bloomer.

entries.clue: Large vehicle upending dirt onto fresh scrap (6,5)

indicatorNotes.upending: in a down clue, upending turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards
indicatorNotes.onto: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of what follows

blocks.note: MUD, upended
fresh = cheeky, pert
a ruck is a scrap, a brawl

annotation.surface: A lorry tipping soil onto a heap of fresh scrap metal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a working tipper lorry, 'upending dirt'. Fresh means cheeky here, and scrap is a fight, not waste metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose description: the site vehicle that tips its load is big, but the definition only gives its size.

entries.clue: Tenner originally put in bucket by coercion, unquestionably (3,7)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally means at the start, so take the first letter of tenner
indicatorNotes.put in: put in means inserted, so T goes inside RAIN
indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so RAIN is placed next to FORCE

blocks.note: force = coercion
to bucket, or bucket down, is to rain hard
first letter of tenner, put inside RAIN

annotation.surface: A ten-pound note dropped into a collecting bucket under duress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bucket' looks like a pail for the tenner, but it is a verb: it's bucketing down. FORCE comes first even though 'by coercion' is last in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean beyond doubt.

entries.clue: Transported to a prison, killer in trap? (3,6)

indicatorNotes.Transported: transported letters are carried off and set down in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A murderer caught in a sting and shipped off to jail.
annotation.walkthrough: The trap is a rodent trap, not a police sting, and the killer is the bait laid in it; the question mark flags that loose sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the toxic bait put in a trap is what kills the vermin.

entries.clue: Reversible brim for Royal Ascot, say? (4)

indicatorNotes.Reversible: something reversible can be turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to brim or teem is to be full to overflowing

annotation.surface: A hat with a two-sided brim worn to Royal Ascot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brim' suggests the brim of a hat, fitting Ascot's famous millinery, but it is the verb: brim with, teem with. Royal Ascot is a summer horse-racing festival in England.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a race meeting such as Royal Ascot is called by this short hunting and racing word.

entries.clue: Sword, the sharp blade broke finally (4)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so take each word's final letter

blocks.note: last letters of thE sharP bladE brokE

annotation.surface: A sword whose keen blade finally snapped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to say when the blade broke; it tells you to take the last letter of each of the four words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the fencing weapon with a stiff blade is one kind of sword.

entries.clue: Machiavellian line penned by children’s author (7)

indicatorNotes.penned by: penned means shut in a pen, so L is enclosed by POTTER

blocks.note: Beatrix Potter, author of Peter Rabbit
L = line

annotation.surface: A children's writer penning a sly, scheming line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like writing, suiting an author, but here it means enclosed, as sheep in a pen. Machiavellian works as a noun: a schemer.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun use: a Machiavellian is a cunning intriguer, one who schemes.

entries.clue: Country’s assorted lotteries taking in millions (5-5)

indicatorNotes.assorted: assorted things are mixed up, so the letters take a new order
indicatorNotes.taking in: taking in means including, so the lotteries include M before being jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder
M = million(s)
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A nation's various lotteries raking in millions.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. The answer is the official name of East Timor.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: East Timor, in south-east Asia, is a sovereign nation.

entries.clue: Christmas away fixture consuming a football boss, say? (7)

indicatorNotes.consuming: consuming means eating up, so the manger swallows the A

blocks.note: from the carol 'Away in a Manger'
taken literally

annotation.surface: A festive away match that swallows up a football manager.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Away fixture' sounds like football, matching the boss, but it points to the carol 'Away in a Manger': the crib is the Christmas fixture.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the boss of a football club is one kind of person in charge, hence 'say'.

entries.clue: Sink to bottom of heap in effect again (7)

indicatorNotes.bottom of: in a down clue, the bottom of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the P is placed inside REDO

blocks.note: taken literally
to effect again is to redo
last letter of heap, placed inside REDO

annotation.surface: Slumping to the bottom of the pile once more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Effect' is a verb here, to bring about, so effecting again is redoing. 'Sink' is a verb too, as in sinking a ship or a plan.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hole a ship below the waterline, or wreck a scheme, is to sink it.

entries.clue: Where urban development has evidently gone with a bang? (4,4)

annotation.definition: Where urban development has evidently gone with a bang?

blocks.note: the surface pushes an explosion, a place blown up
the setter means a settlement that grew in an economic surge

annotation.surface: A town that has grown explosively.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gone with a bang' suggests an explosion, but the bang is an economic surge: a place that grew fast, as in a gold rush.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a rapid economic surge and a loud bang share one word, and the clue plays on both.

entries.clue: Thin, twisted hooks put away (6)

indicatorNotes.hooks: to hook something is to catch and hold it, so the twisted word holds the next one inside

blocks.note: wry = twisted, as a wry neck
to put away food is to eat it

annotation.surface: A thin, bent set of hooks being stored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' looks like an anagram indicator and 'hooks' like a noun; really the first is a synonym and the second a verb meaning to catch and hold.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: soup or tea that is too diluted is thin.

entries.clue: Braid is ’eld by us? (5)

indicatorNotes.’eld: the dropped h tells you to hear the words in a Cockney voice

blocks.note: what is held by us is what we have, said with the h dropped just as the clue drops it from held

annotation.surface: A Cockney asking whether this braid belongs to us.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ’eld is the signal: drop the h from 'we have' as the clue drops it from 'held'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to braid hair or cord is to interlace its strands.

entries.clue: Score mark when difficult game turns, keeping one in match (4,9)

indicatorNotes.difficult: difficult letters are awkward and knotted, so GAME TURNS is rearranged
indicatorNotes.keeping: keeping means holding, so the jumble holds I within it
indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the whole jumble goes inside TIE

blocks.note: a match or cup tie; the rest goes inside it, between I and E
anagram fodder
I = one, joining the fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Recording a score when a tough match swings, one player holding on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a sports scorecard, but the score is sheet music and the mark is something like 4/4 at the start of the stave.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the pair of numbers at the start of a musical score marking beats per bar.

entries.clue: Withdraw first of money that’s been raised in kitty (3)

indicatorNotes.first of: the first of a word is its opening letter, here from money
indicatorNotes.that’s been raised: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: to go is to leave, withdraw
first letter of money

annotation.surface: Taking cash back out of a raised pool of money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a pool of money, fitting the surface, but it is a cat.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: British slang for a cat, short for moggy.

entries.clue: Puff happening — to be one? (6)

blocks.note: a drag is a puff on a cigarette
on = taking place, as in 'what's on'

annotation.surface: Someone smoking and asking whether that makes them a fire-breather.
annotation.walkthrough: Puff also names the creature of the folk song 'Puff, the Magic Dragon', so Puff happens to be one. Read as wordplay, the same Puff is a drag on a cigarette.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit-style reading: Puff of the song is a fire-breathing beast of legend, which is what 'to be one' points at.

entries.clue: Bird on atoll in tangle? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.on: on means next to, so in an across clue the bird follows the atoll

blocks.note: an atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef
the knot is a wading bird

annotation.surface: A seabird on a coral island, caught up in a mess.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tangle' is a loose definition, hence the question mark: a square sailor's tie is a deliberate tangle of rope. Bird comes first in the clue but goes second in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition by example: the sailor's square tie is an ordered tangle of rope.
